title: Class rank within grade level
statementMd:
Rank students within their grade level by average score (1 = best) using `RANK()`. Show grade level, rank, name and average rounded to 1 decimal. Keep ranks 1 to 3, ordered by grade level, rank, name.

Expected columns: `grade_level`, `rk`, `name`, `avg_score`.

Tables: `teachers`, `courses`, `students`, `enrollments`.

**Row order matters** for this problem.
hints: Average per student, then `RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY grade_level ...)`.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH a AS (SELECT s.grade_level, s.name, AVG(e.score) AS avg_score FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY grade_level ORDER BY avg_score DESC) AS rk FROM a) SELECT grade_level, rk, name, ROUND(avg_score, 1) AS avg_score FROM r WHERE rk <= 3 ORDER BY grade_level, rk, name;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
